# Katahdin (04, engineer) — BAD-078

## Brief
Make `test/movecheck.test.js` pass in CI on PR https://github.com/0snug0/BadTakes/pull/381, branch `feat/bad-078-movecheck`. The `test` and `test-windows` jobs are red; `smoke` and `changes` pass.

## The failure

`scripts/movecheck.mjs` reads the pre-split side of every corpus entry out of git history (`git show 5751929^:web/app.js`), which is the right design — it makes a run reproducible and keeps multi-megabyte fixture trees out of the repository. But `actions/checkout@v7` clones shallow by default, so **none of the six corpus revisions exists on the runner** and every history-reading test dies:

```
# fatal: invalid object name '5751929^'.
not ok 1 - BAD-044 — web/app.js (1909 lines) into app-<part>.js classic scripts
    at resolveOld (scripts/movecheck/sources.mjs:81:16)
```

Six corpus tests plus every perturbation test built on `a0baf97`. Job logs: `test` https://github.com/0snug0/BadTakes/actions/runs/35075300160/job/104726228981 and `test-windows` .../104726228942.

There is an irony worth naming, because it is the lesson: the harness deliberately avoided borrowing `admin/node_modules/typescript` on the argument that a committed tool must not die on a fresh clone — and then depended on git history, which a fresh CI clone does not have either. Same class of assumption, different resource.

## The fix, in two parts

**1. Give the two jobs the history.** In `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, the `test` and `test-windows` jobs check out with the action's defaults (around lines 110 and 157 — verify before editing; other jobs share the shape). The `changes` job at line 93 already passes `fetch-depth: 0`, so this repository has the precedent and the spelling. History here is **840 commits, 20 MiB packed**, so a full fetch is cheap; that is why this is the fix rather than something cleverer.

Add a short comment saying *why* the depth is needed — a bare `fetch-depth: 0` is exactly the line a later reader deletes as cargo cult. Something in the register of the file's existing comments, naming that `test/movecheck.test.js` reads pre-split revisions out of history.

Check whether any other workflow runs `npm test` (`grep -rn 'npm test' .github/workflows/`) and needs the same treatment. Do not change jobs that do not need it.

**2. Make the precondition legible when it is absent.** `fatal: invalid object name '5751929^'` tells a reader nothing about what to do. `scripts/movecheck/sources.mjs` (`git()` at :18, `resolveOld` at :81) should recognise that a revision is missing and say so with the remedy: the checkout is shallow or the revision is absent, and `git fetch --unshallow` (or `fetch-depth: 0` in a workflow) is the fix.

**Fail, do not skip.** This repository's own `implementing-changes` skill names silently-skipped tests as a way a green run goes vacuous, and a corpus that quietly does not run is exactly that: the six clean runs are the evidence this tool works at all. A loud failure naming the one command to fix it costs a shallow-clone contributor one command; a silent skip costs everyone the proof. If, having read the code, you think a skip is genuinely right here, say so in your Result with your reasoning and implement the failure anyway — that call is Spud's, not yours to make unilaterally.

Keep the message useful on both platforms; `test-windows` fails identically and must come back green too.

## Outcome
Right fix on both halves, and she did the one thing the brief actually cared about: she did not hand back an error message she had not seen. My brief promised her a git clone into scratch to reproduce the shallow condition, and Law 7's Bash hook refused it — correctly, since the hook holds every caller with an agent_id and knows nothing about scratch. Rather than skip the reproduction or claim it, she named the refusal and substituted a probe that produces the byte-identical failure class: git cannot distinguish a well-formed absent revision from a shallow-omitted object, so pointing resolveOld and resolveTree at an absent rev hits the same path CI hits. That is a sound substitution and she showed her reasoning for it. The brief was mine and it was wrong to promise the clone; the friction is real and worth its own Spud ticket. Her proposal 122 is the valuable find — release.yml checks out shallow at :38 and runs npm test at :47, so this PR as it stood would have planted a landmine under the next tag release. Declining it as a separate ticket and fixing it inside BAD-078, where it belongs: a harness that breaks the release pipeline is not done.
